name: Barnard's Star
summary: Barnard's Star is a small, cool red dwarf about 6 light-years away, the closest single star to the Sun. It is too faint to see without a telescope, but it moves across the sky faster than any other known star.
why_interesting: Its fast apparent motion makes it the perfect test for SkyShift: in SPHEREx images taken months apart you can watch it change position against the background stars.

facts.label: Distance
facts.compare: The light you see from it left the star about 6 years ago.

facts.label: Proper motion
facts.compare: The fastest of any known star: it crosses the width of the full Moon in about 180 years.

facts.label: Mass
facts.compare: About one sixth of the Sun's mass.

facts.label: Size
facts.compare: About one fifth of the Sun's width, roughly twice the size of Jupiter.

facts.label: Temperature
facts.compare: About half as hot as the Sun's surface, which is why it glows red and shines mostly in infrared light.

facts.label: Age
facts.compare: About twice as old as the Sun.

facts.label: Rotation period
facts.compare: The Sun turns once in about 25 days; this old star spins almost 6 times slower.

facts.label: Planets
facts.compare: All four are smaller than Earth.

papers.title: The Barnard's Star planetary system: stability, composition, and evolution of four sub-Earth exoplanets
